claims.statement: The repository is organized as two layers: an engine of skills and agents (skills/, agents/) that does the work, and a harness (feature-intake, hooks/, rules/, specs/<slug>/SUMMARY.md) that decides before the engine runs how much process a change needs and when to involve a human.
The harness principle is that ceremony scales with risk (lane) while human interruption scales with ambiguity/confidence; these are independent dials.

Change flow is request -> /feature-intake -> Lane + Confidence -> route -> build -> hooks corroborate -> ship; intake writes Lane and confidence to specs/<slug>/SUMMARY.md and the lane selects tiny (direct edit), normal (subagent-driven-development) or high-risk (brainstorming -> xia2 -> writing-plans -> build).
Low confidence or a hard gate escalates to a human via specs/<slug>/ESCALATIONS.md with deny-on-no-response, and a hard gate discovered mid-task escalates regardless of the original lane.

settings.json registers four hooks: commit-gate.sh on PreToolUse Bash, branch-isolation-guard.sh on PreToolUse Write|Edit, session-knowledge.sh on SessionStart, and model-config.sh on SessionStart with matcher startup|clear; the manifest hooks list marks all four as wired.

Every lane must cut a branch before the first edit; branch-isolation-guard.sh denies implementation edits on shared branches (HARNESS_SHARED_BRANCHES, default main/master) judged by the checkout owning each edit path, exempting edits whose paths are all under specs/*.

At commit time commit-gate.sh corroborates the declared Lane (from a staged SUMMARY.md, else the active plan's sibling SUMMARY) against the staged diff, so a diff carrying a block-mode hard-gate signal cannot be committed under a lane below high-risk, while warn-mode signals only print a note.

session-knowledge.sh never blocks: it loads critical-patterns and an INDEX pointer from docs/solutions, up to 5 active runs from runtime/run_state.py list --active --json, and the cached Codex runtime-mode context, and exits 0 on every path; it displays but never runs the Codex doctor.

Both PreToolUse hooks normalize Claude and Codex payloads through hooks/lib/normalize-tool-input.py, which distinguishes runtimes by turn_id (Codex) vs session_id (Claude) and parses apply_patch programs into a path set, defaulting to unknown status.
commit-gate.sh resolves per-gate block/warn modes only from the git index (git show :harness-manifest.json) or embedded defaults, never from a worktree or .claude/ copy of the manifest.

harness-manifest.json is the single source of truth for hard-gate slugs and their block/warn modes (workflow-engine and weakening-validation are warn, the rest block), the hook inventory (four wired hooks), hook profiles, the skill list (including diagnosing-bugs and harness-models), the agent roles and binding renderer, and contract surface-to-consumer maps validated by scripts/check_manifest.py.

Hook profiles: minimal installs branch-isolation-guard.sh and commit-gate.sh, standard and strict install all four hooks (adding session-knowledge.sh and model-config.sh), strict runs commit-gate.sh --profile strict, and standard is the default.
Rule loading is two-tier: rule files without paths: frontmatter auto-load every session, while those with paths: load contextually when matching specs/** files are read.

runtime/run_state.py is an event-sourced per-slug state machine storing an append-only specs/<slug>/events.jsonl guarded by an fcntl lock file and an atomically written RUN.json projection rebuildable from the log, with exit codes 0 success, 2 invalid input/transition, 3 storage/chain/projection failure.

Run states are split into active, interrupt (blocked, escalated) and terminal (shipped, cancelled, superseded) sets; waiting states require waiting_on and interrupt states require resume_event, and terminal states allow no transitions.

run_state.py is called at workflow checkpoints by the feature-intake, subagent-driven-development and finishing skills, session-knowledge.sh, scripts/harness-status.sh and the post-merge maintenance workflow.

runtime/runtime_mode.py persists sanitized Codex diagnosis (enforced/advisory/unsupported) to the gitignored .harness-state/codex-runtime.json, and verify_summary.py checks the optional Runtime-mode/Runtime-evidence-id SUMMARY pair only for format.

The root directories are the source of truth and .claude/ is a derived gitignored copy built by scripts/deploy-harness.sh, which syncs skills, agents, hooks, rules, templates, runtime and an allow-listed subset of scripts (including apply_model_config.py) plus harness-manifest.json, while agents/*.json and adapters/ never deploy.

Deploy re-sync merges with consumers' own settings.json hooks and keeps differing consumer-owned files (rules/architecture.md, rules/guidelines.md, rules/behavior.md, agents/PROJECT.md) by writing the incoming copy as <file>.harness-incoming unless --overwrite-conflicts is passed.

Claude Code is the established runtime; the Codex advisory alpha is a generated non-clobber adapter rendering the same skills, agents and hook bodies, not peer enforcement or GA, with complete evidence only for Codex CLI 0.147.0 on macOS arm64.

render_codex_adapter.py derives the Codex hooks.json from settings.json, rewriting commands to bash "$PLUGIN_ROOT/hooks/...", mapping the Write|Edit matcher to apply_patch|Edit|Write, adding additionalContextLimit 2500 to SessionStart handlers, and aborting on unmapped hook events.
The Codex adapter is installed via scripts/install-codex-harness.sh delegating to deploy-codex-adapter.sh and never replaces the Claude .claude/ deployment.

codex_harness_doctor.py runs outside hooks, supports only macos-arm64, and because no current input carries observed hook trust a real run returns advisory or unsupported; an enforced result today is treated as a bug.

evals/ holds fixture-based behavioral evals of skill judgment (intake classifier, review chain, task review, prompt-refactor corpus, test-runner, plus manual context-boundary probes) scored deterministically by scripts where a scorer exists but run manually rather than in CI, distinct from deterministic tests run by scripts/run-tests.sh.
scripts/run-tests.sh is the single CI test entrypoint covering syntax, doc-truth lint, manifest consistency checks, hook contract tests and script integration tests.
Every gate enforces exactly one evidence tier (traceability, provenance, or truth) and new gates must document Verifies: and Does not verify: lines.

scripts/ci-strict-gate.sh blocks PRs touching hooks/, settings.json, templates/ or render_plan.py unless a changed high-risk SUMMARY.md has Verify rows that re-run clean, and only warns for scripts/ changes by default.

model-config.sh is not registered in the Codex adapter: render_codex_adapter.py skips any handler whose command is model-config.sh because it rewrites Claude frontmatter only, so the rendered hooks.json has session-knowledge.sh as its only SessionStart handler.

model-config.sh is a never-blocking SessionStart wrapper that pipes the payload to scripts/apply_model_config.py --hook, which applies the validated harness-models.json model and effort values to the deployed .claude/agents/<role>.md and .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md frontmatter and never writes a settings file.

deploy-harness.sh validates the target's harness-models.json against a defaults snapshot rendered from source before anything under .claude/ is written (aborting on failure, also under --dry-run), and applies it after the derived helper-path rewrite by copying the snapshot to .claude/harness-models.defaults.json and running apply_model_config.py --apply.

When deriving .claude/settings.json, deploy-harness.sh keeps only the hooks named in the selected profile (by command basename), appends --profile

to the commit-gate command, and records the profile in .claude/.harness-profile so a flagless re-sync reuses it.

An Input-type: bug fix request runs diagnosing-bugs before the lane route on every lane; it proves the root cause in specs/<slug>/diagnosis.md through six gated phases, task-reviewer reviews it before any fix, and normal/high-risk lanes take diagnosis.md as input to their chain.
harness-models.json (schema_version 1) sets model and effort per agent role and per skill, and the /harness-models skill shows, checks, or applies it.
